title: Perch: install notice and update keys (/hub/install)
what:
minerva = <canonical dir of the perch exe>/minerva if executable, else --minerva; never a PATH lookup. A perch exe under /nix/store gives {installed:false, managed:'nix'}.
Routes:
- GET /hub/install: from `minerva status --json`; {installed:false, why} without it; never the network, never update
- GET /hub/install/keys: `keys list --json`
- POST /hub/install/keys/inspect {pubkey ≤ 4 KiB}: `keys inspect - --json`, key on stdin
- POST /hub/install/keys/add {pubkey, confirm}
  - confirm is normalized to 16 hex; the guard per D4 (b2: an unexpired arm for exactly that FP, consumed on use)
  - runs `keys add - --confirm <FP> --json`
  - 200 {added}; 409 {why}; 403 {why: 'in a terminal: hoot keys allow-web <FP>, then add within 2 minutes'}
- POST /hub/install/keys/remove {id, confirm}: only keys whose source is 'added by hand' (ruling 6: the installer contract names `keys remove <id> --confirm <FP>`), under the same guard
- POST /hub/install/keys/arm {fingerprint}: bearer only (the cookie gets 403); one arm per FP; 120 s; single use
Fixed argv, key bytes on stdin, 5 s timeout, 64 KiB output cap, one key write at a time.
Never: update, rotation, jev-setup.
tests:
tests/install.rs with fake_minerva logging argv and stdin:
- the key is on stdin and never in argv; --confirm is always present
- a wrong confirm gives 409 and leaves the fake keys dir untouched
- not installed gives installed:false with no child; the nix path gives managed:'nix'
- the notice: newer, equal, corrupt cache
- arm: a cookie gets 403; an arm works once, only for its FP, and not after 120 s (knob shortens it); an add without an arm gets 403
- remove is refused for compiled-in and rotation keys
- no route ever runs update or remove-all
live_check: fake perch on PORT=48111 with fake_minerva in installed and not-installed modes. This box has no real minerva.
risk: This is the trust root of updates. Page-added keys never expire and survive a release-key revocation (keys.rs:337-352). The arm guards only against script in the page's origin. An agent running as your uid can use the keys CLI or read the bearer; G1's keys rows are the only speed bump there.
